The website project

From the page plan
to the finished site.

Your services, words and images become a set of pages that work together. The project covers planning, design, development and handover.

Page planning

An outline of the pages, their content and the routes between them.

Visual design

Layouts, typography, colour and imagery developed around your existing business identity.

Responsive build

Pages that adapt to phones and larger screens, including navigation, images and forms.

Contact routes

Calls, enquiry forms or links to an existing booking service, with delivery checks where forms are included.

SEO foundations

Page titles, descriptions, headings and image optimisation, with technical indexing checks before release.

Review & handover

Design reviews, checks of the finished pages and guidance on the files, accounts and editing setup.

Before we begin

Before the project
begins.

You do not need all the answers at the start. These are some of the details we work through before a build.

Do you offer SEO or digital marketing?

Website projects include SEO foundations such as page titles, headings, image optimisation and technical indexing checks. Ongoing search campaigns, advertising and social media management are outside the current offer. Search positions are not guaranteed.

Do I need finished content?

An outline is enough to begin planning. Before the build, we identify who is preparing the words and images and when they will be ready. You approve the business information and any supplied material.

Can I update the website myself?

Editing needs help determine the build. A content-management system provides an editor for regular changes; a static site may suit content that changes less often. We explain the proposed setup and your editing options before work starts.

How much does it cost, and how long does it take?

The number of pages, features, content work and any existing setup determine the work involved. Your proposal includes a fee and schedule, with the content and review dates needed to keep the project moving. Care and third-party costs are separate.

Who owns the website and accounts?

File ownership, domain and hosting accounts, licences and access handover are agreed before work starts. Any third-party restrictions and recurring charges are identified separately.
